newsitem.title: FRANCE: French train strike disrupts holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: French train strike disrupts holiday weekend.

text.p: A four-day-old strike by French train conductors badly disrupted rail traffic on Saturday, causing misery for thousands of travellers on a long holiday weekend.
The state railway company SNCF said traffic was cut by one third on main lines. High-speed Eurostar trains to London through the Channel tunel were unaffected.
Traffic jams built up on some motorways as holidaymakers switched from trains to cars for the three-day Pentecost weekend.

The strike is to last into Sunday after most conductors voted to reject concessions won by unions in negotiations with the SNCF management. Trains cannot run without conductors, who are responsible for safety as well as checking tickets.

SNCF agreed to promote an extra 860 of the current 10,000 conductors and hire 200 more this year as well as raise their monthly bonus to 900 francs ($155) from 700 francs ($120) by year-end and to 1,000 francs ($170) early next year.
The hardline Sud-Rail union said concessions fell far short of demands. SNCF, apologising to travellers, said prolonging the strike was injustifiable and would badly hurt the company.
The conductors staged a similar strike last month in another sign of opposition to austerity policies of the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
